Docs.summary: The access mode whose access is specified by the corresponding method VarHandle.get

Docs.summary: The access mode whose access is specified by the corresponding method VarHandle.set
Docs.value: The mode for a plain write, with no cross-thread ordering guarantee. A plain write of Java long or double need not be atomic on a 32-bit platform. Read-only variables do not support writes; check for a handle.

remarks.para: The access mode whose access is specified by the corresponding method VarHandle.set

Docs.summary: The access mode whose access is specified by the corresponding method VarHandle.setOpaque
Docs.value: The mode for an atomic write that is coherently ordered with accesses to the same variable, without release ordering for other variables. Read-only variables do not support writes; check for a handle.

remarks.para: The access mode whose access is specified by the corresponding method VarHandle.setOpaque

Docs.summary: The access mode whose access is specified by the corresponding method VarHandle.setRelease
Docs.value: The mode for an atomic write with release ordering, which orders preceding accesses before a matching acquire read and its subsequent accesses. Read-only variables do not support writes; check for a handle.

remarks.para: The access mode whose access is specified by the corresponding method VarHandle.setRelease

Docs.summary: The access mode whose access is specified by the corresponding method VarHandle.setVolatile
Docs.value: The mode for an atomic write with volatile ordering. Volatile operations are totally ordered with respect to each other. Read-only variables do not support writes; check for a handle.

remarks.para: The access mode whose access is specified by the corresponding method VarHandle.setVolatile
